Here's what Rahmanullah Gurbaz has to say (and this is not verbatim): "After 3-4 
matches I didn't score, I was hungry for a score. I always try to score but luck was 
against me, but today luck was with me. I always try to enjoy my innings. I think it's a 
batting pitch. I worked hard in the last few days on my balance and position. Today I 
was 100 per cent focussed. I can give credit to captain and coach for backing me in 
hard situations. Even if I don't score, they always back me. I think we have enough runs 
on the board. We could have done a little bit more. But we have a good bowling attack 
so we will be happy." 
6.10pm So the 256-run stand, Afghanistan's highest partnership in ODIs, between 
Gurbaz and Zadran set Afghanistan up for a big total, but once Shakib broke that stand, 
the Afghan batters were all in a hurry to get out. Ibrahim Zadran stayed steady and 
reached his century but was out right after as he tried to take on the bowling. 
Bangladesh will be happy with the comeback they made, but their target is ten more 
than their biggest ever chase. Another point of concern for Bangladesh will be the injury 
to Ebadot Hossain, who twisted his knee after his run-up was disrupted while bowling 
his final over. 
Plenty of records broken, mainly by Gurbaz and Zadran. Apart from their record
